 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Ipswich's return to the top flight has been relatively inconsistent. Sitting 14th with 11 points, the Tractor Boys have shown they possess enough quality to compete, but defensive vulnerabilities have prevented them from establishing any real momentum.
 Gary O'Neil's side have struggled for consistency in recent weeks, with back-to-back draws against Nottingham Forest and Hull City leaving them without a league victory in three matches.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Their attacking output has been encouraging, though. Ipswich have demonstrated an ability to recover from difficult positions, collecting eight Premier League points from losing positions, highlighting their resilience.
 Sportimage
 In terms of players to watch, there are two main ones for Ipswich. Firstly, Julio Enciso has arguably been Ipswich's biggest attacking threat since arriving from Strasbourg. His creativity, ability to operate between the lines and willingness to attempt shots from distance make him a constant danger. His spectacular strike against Hull demonstrated exactly what he can produce.
 Secondly is their midfielder Exequiel Palacios, who signed from Bayer Leverkusen in the summer provides quality and composure in the middle of the park. His ability to receive possession under pressure, dictate tempo and progress the ball makes him particularly important against teams that press aggressively.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement AFCB supporters will remember O'Neil's pragmatic approach during his time on the south coast, and Ipswich have adopted some similar characteristics.
 He has primarily favoured a 4-2-3-1 formation, with two holding midfielders providing protection for the back four. Against stronger opposition, Ipswich can become more conservative, dropping into a compact low block or even switching to a 5-4-1.
 Mark Pain
 The Cherries should look to impose their usual intensity from the opening whistle. Marco Rose's side have developed considerable attacking momentum, and playing at a high tempo could cause Ipswich significant problems.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bournemouth should look to exploit the spaces between Ipswich's midfield and defensive lines. Getting Justin Kluivert and Marcus Tavernier involved in those pockets could be particularly effective, while Evanilson's movement and hold-up play should create opportunities for Rayan to attack the spaces around the penalty area.
 Tyler Adams and Ryan Christie must be switched on defensively. Allowing Palacios too much time on the ball could make it difficult to maintain control, while Enciso's ability to produce moments of individual brilliance cannot be underestimated.
 Every Second Media
 In conclusion, Ipswich are a side with genuine attacking threats but clear defensive weaknesses. Bournemouth's recent form will make them favourites, and if they can maintain their intensity, move the ball quickly and take advantage of Ipswich's defensive uncertainty, there is every reason to believe they can leave Portman Road with another three points.
